# R355 — decode phase-cache fill/readback cost and 24-output amortization

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/arithmetic investigation for the unbuilt phase-cache candidate. Scope: 912-slot decode residency under the unchanged upstream 24-output stock workload; fill/readback, retirement/reinit, hardware transfer ceilings, and next observations. No test, import, AST tool, build, GPU/model/profiler/process/service query, Git operation, source edit, registry edit, or cleanup was performed. The only new artifact is this report. Estimates below are conditional ceilings/lower bounds, not performance measurements or an adoption recommendation.

## Finding

The additional 768 blobs are charged once after every successful fresh GEN prompt. This remains true for the stock client's short warm-up request: source runs the same prompt completion, producer/compute retirement, Prefill reset, VMM extra mapping, full extra fill/readback/byte comparison, and residency publication before its decode windows. The candidate's source timestamp for `prompt_ms` is taken before `successful_prompt()` executes, so the added phase treatment is omitted from the engine's reported `prompt_ms`; `decode_ms` starts later, after refill. Both reported engine timing fields therefore omit this treatment. A stock-bench row's enclosing request/wall clock should include it; confirm that aggregation in the candidate run rather than relying on engine `prompt_ms` or `decode_ms` alone.

At the source-level copy path, each of the 768 expert blobs is written to device, read back to a host verification buffer, and compared byte-for-byte. `gpu::copy` enqueues one `queue.memcpy` and synchronously waits; `fill_checked` calls it separately for write and read. This is 1,536 synchronous copy/wait operations, plus 768 CPU `memcmp`s, after mapping. It is not a single overlapped batch. The source logs one combined `fill_check_ms` spanning map, all transfers, comparisons, publication and refresh, while retirement and reinitialization have separate partial logs. It does not log distinct byte counts/times for H2D, D2H, memcmp, map, Prefill reset, or the full request wall increment.

## Payload and transport bounds

The implementation uses the actual layer `blob_bytes` for each filled slot, so exact candidate bytes are `16 * sum(blob_bytes[layer] for 48 layers)`. No built/candidate runtime layout or exact 48-layer sum is available. A retained former-route report records one layer's 512-expert cache as 1,363,148,800 bytes, or 2,662,400 bytes/expert; a separate compact IQ3_S layer fixture records 2,329,600 bytes. These are useful scale points, not proof of this candidate's loaded-pack layer sizes. Applying those endpoints to 768 additions gives a conditional payload range of 1.790–2.044 GB in each direction.

| Conditional quantity | 2.3296 MB/blob case | 2.6624 MB/blob case |
|---|---:|---:|
| 768 additional source blobs | 1.790 GB | 2.044 GB |
| Write + readback PCIe payload | 3.579 GB | 4.089 GB |
| Ideal serialized time at installed Gen4 x4 encoded ceiling (7.8769 GB/s) | 0.454 s | 0.519 s |
| Time at prior, unverified ~6 GB/s planning figure | 0.596 s | 0.681 s |

The installed external path is Gen4 x4; 7.8769 GB/s is the encoding-only ceiling, not application throughput. The earlier ~6 GB/s value lacks a current raw receipt and is only a planning scenario. The source synchronously completes each H2D copy before its D2H readback, so concurrent bidirectional transfer is not a source-supported assumption. Real time must be above the applicable byte serialization floor and will also contain per-copy wait/launch overhead, mapping, verification, publication, retirement, and workspace reinitialization. Conversely, actual layer blob bytes may fall outside the fixture endpoints; Main must log exact bytes.

For 24 outputs, the transport-only floor corresponds to 18.9–21.6 ms/output at encoded line rate, or 24.8–28.4 ms/output at the provisional 6 GB/s rate. If a 24-token decode otherwise takes 2.64–2.93 s at the reported 9.1–8.2 tok/s, adding only that scenario transfer time gives about 7.0–7.8 tok/s at line rate, or 6.6–7.4 tok/s at 6 GB/s. This is arithmetic sensitivity only: baseline timing is not guaranteed to exclude/contain any corresponding cache work, and CPU hit savings may recover part or all of it. It shows that a measured decode-only improvement must save around 0.45–0.68 s per request just to cover the transport floor in end-to-end latency; actual threshold is higher before CPU miss work saved is credited.

The previous source-derived 1.363 GB full-layer figure is not this candidate's measured VMM allocation. Candidate's mapping size, retained physical bytes and actual free-memory deltas are explicitly logged at runtime and must be kept separate from blob payload: alignment/granularity padding increases mapped/physical bytes but is not useful transfer payload. The Arc B570's 380 GB/s advertised GDDR bandwidth is not the limit for these host-device copies; PCIe is the applicable upper bound. No current local sustained device-memory bandwidth or exact GPU/CPU overlap measurement changes this conclusion.

## Cost placement and amortization semantics

The request lifecycle in `generate.cpp` is: finish prompt and CPU jobs; record `phase_prompt_finished`; perform `successful_prompt()` (wait/retire producer and compute work, snapshot stats/free memory, destroy/release `Prefill::Impl` and its lazy GEMM scratch, map extras, fill/readback/compare all 768, upload/check residency and refresh); then emit prompt timing and run decode. Before the next GEN, the source invalidates extra residency, uploads/checks it, unmaps and destroys extras, and reinitializes the same Prefill workspace. QUIT has its own checked owner-close lifecycle. Thus:

- `prompt_ms` currently stops before the phase fill and workspace retirement; `decode_ms` starts after it. The upstream client's request-level wall latency/elapsed time is needed for the full cost.
- Every successful GEN, including warm-up, pays the one-time-per-request fill/readback. It is not amortized across the 24 output tokens in the engine's decode rate.
- Within the request, the potential benefit is only the avoided CPU service for routed expert misses. If `h` is the extra-cache hit fraction among eligible expert dispatches and `C_miss` is the marginal critical-path CPU miss service per dispatch, the maximum service avoided is bounded by `h * N_dispatch * C_miss`, further reduced by overlap with GPU work. Break-even requires the measured end-to-end avoided critical path to exceed the measured map/fill/readback/publish + retire/reinit increment. Logical blob bytes or summed host worker spans cannot substitute for `C_miss` or critical-path time.
- Profile membership is fixed to the first 19 ranked experts/layer (3 baseline + 16 additional). 912 slots mean capacity/membership, not 912 guaranteed hits. Existing ~1.8% cache-hit observation belongs to the previous 144-cache route and is not the 16-extra profile's expected hit rate.

A CPU memory traffic scale check also cautions against assuming readback validation is free. For the conditional 1.79–2.04 GB payload, the source reads the host source for H2D; D2H writes the verification buffer; `memcmp` then reads both buffers. This is roughly 3.6–4.1 GB PCIe plus up to 7.2–8.2 GB of host-buffer memory operations at the algorithmic level, with caching and implementation effects unknown. The 5600X system's DDR4 theoretical bandwidth is not a measured sustained rate here; do not convert these bytes into a latency prediction. CPU decode miss costs from older pool counters are overlapping worker elapsed time, not exclusive per-miss service and cannot yet be used to assert cache break-even.

## Candidate priority from present evidence

1. **First priority: collect full-lifecycle attribution and the 24-output end-to-end OFF/ON stock rows on the new binary, only after Main's prescribed qualification gates.** Save exact `sum(blob_bytes)`, selected expert count/hit/miss/CPU jobs, map count/bytes, fill and readback bytes/times separately, memcmp time, publish, Prefill reset/reinit, detach, each request wall and its engine `prompt_ms`/`decode_ms`. Include the short warm-up as a charged request. This resolves the largest missing number and prevents an apparent engine decode-rate gain from being mistaken for end-to-end benefit.
2. **Use measured rank hit rate and service value to decide whether 16 extras/layer are worth their per-request transfer tax.** The present records establish neither the profile's actual hit rate nor marginal CPU-miss critical path under the stock 24-output workload. At a 9 tok/s decode, the transport-only floor is already roughly 17–26% of a 24-token decode span; a high miss fraction with costly serialized service could pay it back, while low hit credit cannot.
3. **Only then compare a smaller quota or different ranked cutoff as a candidate design.** Do not presume linear scaling: fewer slots reduce copy bytes roughly with quota, but cache hit rate and avoided CPU jobs can be strongly rank-dependent. Any changed quota is a distinct source/binary/quality/runtime comparison and the current candidate intentionally has no reduced-capacity fallback.
4. **Do not rank internal GDN Q/K/V/Y kernel deletion ahead of this attribution based on the current evidence.** R350 corrected the Y-removal proposal; prior max-region winners depend on the active GDN region. The current cache candidate changes ownership/residency and needs its own lifecycle proof first. Do not alter quantization/state precision in this comparison; that is a separate quality gate.

No candidate is shown to improve current ~9 tok/s. The defensible conclusion is that phase cache has a meaningful per-GEN lower-bound toll, likely visible in stock-bench request wall but hidden from reported prompt/decode components, and that 24 outputs give limited amortization. Savings from CPU misses remain unknown, so hardware arithmetic cannot rank 912 above 144 as a net speed win.

## Next observation set

After qualification and under Main's exclusive measurement window, pair fresh OFF/ON stock rows with identical prompt/output settings and report individual samples. For each ON GEN capture: exact per-layer blob bytes and rank pairs; `n_fill=768`; H2D and D2H successful bytes and elapsed spans; synchronous wait count; readback comparison bytes/time; VMM extent count/physical mapped bytes; pre/post-retirement free VRAM; reset and reinit spans; invalidation/detach; `host_residency` and `device_residency` check outcome; expert dispatches by rank, hits, CPU-served misses and per-job/per-phase worker data; total request wall. Keep engine prompt/decode values as separate clocks and compare their sum with wall to locate the omitted intervals; do not add nested CPU worker spans to wall. Record failed copy/readback/fault/correctness cases without treating them as timing samples.

Minimum useful discriminator: enough same-process GEN cycles to observe warm-up cost and following measured request separately, plus multiple independent process pairs for variability; preserve source, binary/provider identity and each sample as Main requires. The decisive output is delta full request wall per 24 generated tokens versus delta decode wall, alongside hit/miss and copy accounting. If fill bytes/time dominate and hit credit is modest, stop increasing cache quota. If the cache sharply cuts CPU-served miss critical path by more than the measured phase toll and full request wall falls, the candidate earns further study. This is an observation rule, not a pre-judged outcome.

## Sources reviewed

- Candidate source, W `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`: `src/program/generate.cpp` phase admission and fill cycle (around lines 4134–4195, 4472–4557, 7970–8040, 9450–9464, 9496, 10248); `src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp` fill/readback/compare/publish; `src/core/gpu.cpp` synchronous `copy`; `src/core/phase_cache_backend.cpp` SYCL `queue.memcpy` backend. Source is edited, unbuilt and untested; no runtime behavior is claimed.
- R347 `research-phase-cache-stock-bench-admission-round347-v1.txt`: stock-client sequence/qualification constraints.
- R207 `round207-gpu-vram-pcie-ceilings-and-prefill-demand.txt`: B570 10 GB, 380 GB/s spec, installed external Gen4 x4 7.8769 GB/s encoding ceiling, caveat on old ~6 GB/s planning figure.
- `decode-retained-vram-after-first-prefill-round10.txt`: historical 1,363,148,800-byte layer cache, former route only.
- `research-full262144-context-runtime-boundary-admission-latest-round223-v1.txt`: compact IQ3_S fixture 2,329,600-byte blob example; not current pack proof.
- `research-upstream-benchsh-decode-measurement-round342-v1.txt`: stock `--long --runs N` uses repeated fresh prompts and up to 24 outputs; not a sustained decode sample.
- R350 correction/report `research-gdn-y-kernel-consumer-alias-round350-v1.txt`: GDN Y-removal proposal corrected; no reuse of the rejected assumption.

No external sources were needed; all numeric hardware ceilings came from the existing primary-source-backed R207 report. No exact current candidate payload, transfer rate, phase duration, CPU miss unit cost, or full-wall speed was measured.
